passage:
Tuesday. Yash saw Gurleen, the senior quality lead, open last month’s inspection file after office hours. A line about a failed check now read “passed.” Yash said nothing and went back to his desk.
Thursday. The team met behind closed doors twice. When Yash went in for coffee, the talk stopped. Everyone studied their cups, and nobody looked at anyone.
Monday. Yash had spent the weekend unsure. Then he wrote down the dates and the file name and asked the compliance officer for a private talk. He kept to facts. “I may be wrong,” he said, “but I want it looked at.” The officer listened, thanked him and said the file would be checked. In the corridor Gurleen passed him and didn’t meet his eyes.

qa.q: What had changed in the inspection file that Yash saw on Tuesday?
qa.a: A line about a failed check now read “passed.”

qa.q: What was Yash feeling over the weekend before he asked for a private talk?
qa.a: Yash was unsure and uneasy, weighing whether he had seen correctly and what speaking up might cost. His careful notes and his words, I may be wrong, show doubt alongside a wish to act.

qa.q: What made Yash's approach to the compliance officer sensible?
qa.a: Yash wrote down dates and the file name, kept to facts and admitted he might be wrong. That gave the compliance officer something checkable rather than an accusation.

qa.q: What might Gurleen have been feeling when passing Yash without meeting his eyes?
qa.a: Gurleen may have felt uneasy or guilty, or simply awkward at the silence in the team. The passage does not say what Gurleen knew, so this is a guess.

grounding: Shows a team member noticing altered documents and closed-door meetings and deciding whom to tell.

passage:
Bhavna, sit down. When I was a junior clerk at a bank branch, I noticed a clerk correcting ledger pages after the auditors’ call. I’m Uday, and I was twenty-four then. The manager shut his door. The tea boy stopped his rounds. Nobody in the room spoke, and Mr. Sinha, the old cashier, kept looking at his hands.
That night I did not sleep. Next morning I wrote down dates and page numbers and went to the audit head. I said, “I saw pages corrected after the call. I don’t know why.”
Weeks later Mr. Sinha told me he’d been waiting for someone younger to speak first.

qa.q: What did Uday notice after the auditors' call?
qa.a: Uday noticed a clerk correcting ledger pages after the auditors' call.

qa.q: What might Mr. Sinha have been feeling as he kept looking at his hands?
qa.a: Mr. Sinha may have felt uneasy and afraid for his position, and unwilling to be the first to speak. His words weeks later, that he was waiting for someone younger, suggest it weighed on him.

qa.q: Which choice did Uday make the next morning, and why was it careful?
qa.a: Uday wrote down dates and page numbers and went to the audit head, saying what was seen and admitting not knowing why. That gave facts without accusation.

qa.q: What might the manager have felt when shutting his door?
qa.a: The manager was probably worried about the branch being found out and wanted to avoid being overheard. The passage shows only the closed door.

grounding: An elder recalls watching pages quietly altered at a bank branch, the silent room, and choosing to speak to the audit head.
